Siddha tradition

Concept of Vatham, Pitham & Kabam

Siddha tradition describes Vatham, Pitham, and Kabam as three principles used to discuss balance in health. This historical framework is part of Siddha practice; it does not replace medical testing or an individual clinical diagnosis.

VathamTraditionally associated with movement
PithamTraditionally associated with transformation
KabamTraditionally associated with structure

Traditional breathing practice · Learning guide

Nasagra Mudra

A traditional hand position used in alternate-nostril breathing. This learning guide presents the practice as a cultural and wellness tradition, not as a treatment or cure for disease.

“வளி, அழல், ஐயம் சமநிலையில் இருந்தால் ஆரோக்கியம்; அவை சீர்கெட்டால் நோய்.”

About the practice

In descriptions of Nasagra Mudra, the thumb rests near one nostril while the ring and little fingers rest near the other. Some traditions use Vishnu Mudra, folding the index and middle fingers into the palm. The left hand may rest comfortably on the knee. Hand positions vary across teachers and traditions.

How it is traditionally described

  1. Sit in a comfortable position and keep the breath natural.
  2. If a qualified instructor has shown you the technique, gently close one nostril and breathe through the other without straining.
  3. Do not force, hold, or deliberately deepen the breath. Stop and rest if you feel dizzy, uncomfortable, or short of breath.

Benefits and evidence

People may explore breathing practices for general wellbeing or as part of yoga. Research on yoga and breathing techniques varies, and this practice should not be presented as a cure for a medical condition or used in place of medical care.

Safety and guidance

Learn from a qualified instructor. If you have a health condition, are pregnant, are older, or have concerns about whether breath practice is suitable for you, discuss it with your healthcare provider first. Avoid forceful breathing and stop if you feel unwell.

NCCIH: Yoga effectiveness and safety ↗Cambridge University Hospitals: Breathing exercises ↗

Please note: This is general educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan. Do not delay medical assessment or stop a prescribed treatment to try a breathing practice.
